handbook-scribelectern-views-text:
The Lectern has four tabs, switched via the icon buttons in the right-hand sidebar.

Read — Shows all tasks and notes as a scrollable list. Any player can read, pin, and check off tasks, even while another player holds the editor lock.

Task Editor — Full document editing. Add tasks, edit text, pin rows, reorder by drag, and delete rows. Changes autosave as you type. Only one player may edit at a time.

Pinned — Lists all of your pinned tasks across every Lectern, fully editable in place. Completions apply immediately with no undo delay.

Settings — Opens the Scribe Settings panel (same as the gear icon on the Pinned Task HUD).
handbook-scribelectern-hud-text:
Hover a task row in Read or Edit view and click the pin icon to add it to your Pinned Task HUD — an always-on overlay showing your pinned tasks over the game world. Pins are per-player; pinning a task on a shared Lectern only affects your own HUD.

Checking off a task from the HUD starts a 1.5-second undo window. During that window the task text fades as a countdown and unchecking cancels the action entirely. After the window elapses the completion is applied according to your chosen policy (keep pinned, unpin, sink to bottom, or delete the task). These policies also apply to completed tasks in the Lectern.

Press P (rebindable under Controls: Scribe Mod) or click the Pinned header to shrink the HUD. Position and size are configurable in Scribe Settings.
craftinginfo-scribe-getting-started-text:
What is Scribe?
Scribe adds a Lectern block for writing tasks and notes and pinning them to a persistent HUD overlay visible while you play.

Crafting the Lectern
See the Scribe Lectern page for the recipe.

Opening the Lectern
Right-click to open in Read view. Shift+right-click to open in Edit view and request the editor lock.

The four views
Read: scroll, complete, and pin tasks to your HUD.
Task Editor: also add, edit, reorder, and delete rows. One player edits at a time.
Pinned: all your pins across every Lectern, editable in place.
Settings: all Scribe preferences.

Pinned Task HUD
Hover a task in Read or Edit view and click the pin icon. The task appears on your HUD immediately. Check it off from the HUD to start the 1.5-second undo window; let it elapse to apply your completion policy.

Press P (rebindable) or click the ▾ Pinned header to collapse the HUD.

For keyboard shortcuts and text editing mechanics, see Scribe Mod: Editor Reference in the handbook.
craftinginfo-scribe-editor-reference-tex:
The following functionality is available on the Lectern.

Row navigation
Tab — move to the next row.
Shift+Tab — move to the previous row.
Enter — insert a new empty task.
Shift+Enter — insert a hard line break within the current row.
Esc — commit and close the Lectern.

Caret movement
Arrow keys — move one character or line.
Alt/Option+Left/Right — skip by whole word.
Cmd+Left/Right (macOS) or Home/End — jump to line start or end.
Ctrl+Left/Right (Windows) — skip by whole word.
Hold Shift with any movement key to extend the selection.

Selection and clipboard
Ctrl/Cmd+A — select all text in the focused field.
Ctrl/Cmd+C — copy. Ctrl/Cmd+X — cut. Ctrl/Cmd+V — paste.
Typing while text is selected replaces the selection.

Empty task behaviour
When you move focus away from a task row (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Esc, or clicking elsewhere), the row is committed. If the row is empty or whitespace-only it is automatically deleted and focus moves to the row above. An empty row that still has focus is not deleted.

On commit, trailing blank lines and trailing whitespace are trimmed from a non-empty row. Interior line breaks (from Shift+Enter) are preserved.

Adding tasks
New Task button — always at the bottom of the Editor.
Enter — inserts a task directly below the current row. Both create an empty row ready to type into immediately.
